verdicts.title: ParallelPoisson inner-mechanism guard added by #850 lives only in the factory, so direct construction and deserialization bypass it and fail later with a self-contradictory message
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree. _parallel_poisson.py:24-38 `ParallelPoisson.__post_init__` validates only `num_workers` and `inner.truncated_batch_size`; the `Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate()` match sits only in the `parallel_poisson()` factory at :131-140. I ran: `parallel_poisson(eps_delta(0.3), 0.1, 2)` -> InputTypeError 'parallel_poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, got EpsDelta.' (guard fires), while `ParallelPoisson(inner=poisson(eps_delta(0.3), 0.1), num_workers=4)` constructs fine, `opaque.serialization.state_dict`/`from_state_dict` round-trips it fine, and both `.pld()` and `.epsilon_at(1e-5)` then raise 'ParallelPoisson requires a Poisson inner mechanism, got Poisson.' - a message that names the wrapper it did receive instead of the unsupported innermost mechanism (EpsDelta). The cited convention is real: _poisson.py:68-72 carries the comment saying truncation pairing is validated in __post_init__ 'so direct construction and deserialization can't ... fail at PLD time', and the `poisson()` factory docstring repeats it. No upstream guard blocks the bypass: `Poisson.__post_init__` only requires the inner to be a `DpProcess`, which `EpsDelta` is, and the process codec used by from_state_dict reconstructs via the dataclass, not the factory. Severity stays low: this is validation placement plus a misleading message. It fails closed and loudly - no wrong epsilon is ever produced - so there is no privacy impact; the cost is a late, confusing error rather than a silent one.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Verified on the current tree (12146ec4 library code): `ParallelPoisson(inner=poisson(eps_delta(0.3), 0.1), num_workers=4)` constructs without error even though the `parallel_poisson()` factory rejects the same inner with InputTypeError, and a `state_dict`/`from_state_dict` round-trip of that object also succeeds. The error is deferred to `.pld()` / `.epsilon_at()`, where it surfaces as `InputTypeError: ParallelPoisson requires a Poisson inner mechanism, got Poisson.` - self-contradictory, because the real problem is the EpsDelta two levels down. Impact is limited to a late and confusing failure (accounting still fails closed, never returning an unsound epsilon); a saved accountant state with an unsupported inner reloads silently and dies on the first epsilon query.

verdicts.title: #850 reintroduced a reference to the removed `random_allocation` API and narrowed the documented plain-Poisson sample_rate range below what the code accepts
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves check out. (1) `git show 3b22a6af -- docs/user-guide/accounting.md` shows exactly the claimed hunk: '`k_out_of_t`, use deterministic transforms' -> '`random_allocation` and `k_out_of_t`, use deterministic transforms', now at docs/user-guide/accounting.md:586. `git show fc44ec8d --stat` confirms the deletion of the Python accountant and sampler modules (216 and 225 lines) plus their test file. At HEAD `grep -rn random_allocation` over all Python sources finds no public symbol: the only survivors are the private Rust function `random_allocation_gaussian_pld` (packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs, reached internally by `k_out_of_t` and `balls_in_bins` through core/_random_allocation_cache.py) and the unrelated third-party cross-validation package of the same name in a test. So docs/user-guide/accounting.md:586 names a non-existent user-facing mechanism. (2) docs/reference/accounting.md:236 does say plain-Poisson `sample_rate` is 'in (0, 1)', while `_poisson.py:49` is `if not 0 < sample_rate <= 1` and `Poisson.pld` has an explicit `sample_rate == 1.0` passthrough branch. I executed it: `poisson(gaussian(1.1), sample_rate=1.0)` constructs and `(step*10).epsilon_at(1e-5)` returns 15.78. Both are documentation-only defects, no code behavior change, hence low. Worth noting to the fix author: 11 lines further down the same file has the inverse error - docs/reference/accounting.md:274 documents `parallel_poisson`'s sample_rate as '(0, 1]', but the factory raises ConfigurationError at 1.0 ('q=1 (full participation on every worker) is not supported here'), which I also ran. I did not treat that as part of this finding but the same edit should fix it. Not a duplicate of the open docs umbrella #775 / #845, which covers citation verification rather than stale API names.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Two verified documentation defects, no runtime impact. docs/user-guide/accounting.md:586 lists `random_allocation` as a mechanism that 'uses deterministic transforms'; no such public API exists at HEAD (fc44ec8d/#761 deleted both the accountant and the sampler; only a private Rust helper keeps the name), so a reader trying `dpsgd_acc.random_allocation(...)` gets an AttributeError. docs/reference/accounting.md:236 documents plain-Poisson `sample_rate` as '(0, 1)' while the code accepts `(0, 1]` and has a documented q=1 passthrough - executed: `poisson(gaussian(1.1), 1.0)` works and `(step*10).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 15.78 - so a reader may avoid the supported no-amplification configuration. Adjacent, not claimed by the finding but verified: docs/reference/accounting.md:274 has the inverse error for `parallel_poisson` ('(0, 1]' documented, 1.0 actually raises ConfigurationError).

verdicts.title: opaque_accounting.pyi declares two native functions the compiled extension does not export
verdicts.reasoning: Verified directly, without rebuilding: I AST-parsed packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.pyi (38 top-level def/class names) and diffed against the loaded extension's public `dir()` (36 names). stub-only = ['balls_in_bins_gaussian_pld', 'balls_in_bins_gaussian_pld_epochs']; runtime-only = [] - exactly the claimed asymmetry, matching the finding's independently built result. Source side agrees: `grep -rn balls_in_bins --include=*.rs packages/opaque-accounting/src/python/` returns nothing, so there is no `#[pyfunction]` and no `m.add_function(...)` registration for either name anywhere in the binding layer (the Rust balls-in-bins code is exposed only through `bnb_mc_pld`-style entries). Stub entries live at lines 392 and 413 of the .pyi. No parity test exists. Severity low and arguably lower than that: `_native` is a private alias used only inside opaque, the two names are unreachable from any public facade, and the failure mode is a type-checker false-negative for a contributor touching the private extension - not a user-visible or privacy-relevant defect. The finding's own framing of this as pre-existing drift (not introduced by #850) is accurate.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Verified: the hand-maintained PyO3 stub packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.pyi declares `balls_in_bins_gaussian_pld` (:392) and `balls_in_bins_gaussian_pld_epochs` (:413), and neither is registered in packages/opaque-accounting/src/python/ nor present in the loaded extension (stub-minus-runtime = exactly those two; runtime-minus-stub = empty). A contributor writing `_native.balls_in_bins_gaussian_pld(...)` inside opaque type-checks clean and fails at runtime with AttributeError. No public facade reaches these names, so no user-facing or accounting-correctness impact; the defect is stale internal type information plus the absence of any stub/runtime parity check.

verdicts.title: torch_compile=True aborts DP training on the first step for every supported dense HF causal-LM family: the now-default fused loss-only CE forward is not Dynamo-traceable under fullgraph=True
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced live on this tree (CPU, torch 2.14.0, transformers 5.15.1) and every link in the chain checked by hand. Reachability: DPTrainer calls `apply_model_patches(..., performance=True, ...)` unconditionally at _dp_trainer.py:844-849 (performance is a literal True, NOT `use_performance_kernels`, whose default is False) and _factory.py:374-376 makes `enable_fused_linear_ce` inherit that True, so the fused causal-LM forward wrapper is installed on all 17 entries of `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM` (cross_entropy.py:122-140) at defaults, on every device. The training path sets the marker: _dp_trainer.py:2437-2442 adds `loss_only=True` when `not return_logits and self._compute_loss_func is None and self._fused_forward_uses_marker`. Compilation is strict with no fallback: `_grad_compiler` (:4337-4370) returns `lambda fn: _compile_strict_chunk(...)` and `_compile_strict_chunk` (:209-219) is `torch.compile(fn, backend=..., mode=..., fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)`; the engine applies it at _clipped_fun.py:723-730 with no try/except, and CPU is a supported compile device (`_recommended_compile_backend` returns 'inductor' for cpu/cuda/mps), so the flag is live on CPU too. Repro: a real `LlamaForCausalLM` (vocab 32, 1 layer) in DPTrainer with `torch_compile=True, torch_compile_backend='aot_eager'`, batch 3, 3 steps -> marker True, then `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: logging.Logger method not supported for non-export cases`, developer context `<Logger transformers.configuration_utils>.warning_once, args: ['`use_return_dict` is deprecated! Use `return_dict` instead!']`, traceback through _clipped_fun.py:601 `vmapped(...)`. Root cause confirmed at cross_entropy.py:257-259 (`return_dict if return_dict is not None else self.config.use_return_dict`) against transformers/configuration_utils.py:210-212, where `use_return_dict` is a property whose body is `logger.warning_once(...)`. Note that line sits BEFORE the CUDA/CPU kernel branch, so the first blocker is device-independent. A/B isolation, all run: Qwen2ForCausalLM -> identical failure; the same Llama run with `performance_kernels_config={'fused_linear_cross_entropy': False}` -> marker False, 3/3 steps, TrainOutput returned; Phi3ForCausalLM (absent from `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM`) -> marker False, 3/3 steps. Second blocker also reproduced: monkeypatching `use_return_dict` to a plain attribute read makes the next graph break `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: ... skipped ... torch._C._functorch...is_gradtrackingtensor`, i.e. `_vmap_batch_factor` at _linear_ce_chunked.py:96 reached from `_tile_plan` at :120. All four cited commits exist with the cited subjects (c0f95ced #988, fae93a55 #979, afa0247f #989, 0a002a50 #990). Docs do advertise the flag: docs/reference/transformers.md:218 and docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:216 both describe torch_compile with fullgraph=True and flag only gradient_checkpointing as incompatible. Test-gap claim verified: test_compile_and_kernel_args.py uses `nn.Linear` (:46) and a hand-written `_TinyLM` (:56-67), neither of which receives the family patch. Severity high, not critical: the failure is loud on step 1, needs the opt-in `torch_compile=True`, and has no epsilon or numerical-correctness consequence - but it is a total outage of a documented feature across every supported dense family, with no fallback and no error message pointing at the cause. Not present in either open-issue list (the perf-audit issues #956-#970 cover kernel throughput, not compile breakage).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Verified by live repro on this tree (CPU, torch 2.14.0, transformers 5.15.1): `DPTrainer(model=LlamaForCausalLM(tiny cfg), args=TrainingArguments(torch_compile=True, torch_compile_backend='aot_eager', use_cpu=True, per_device_train_batch_size=3, max_steps=3, ...)).train()` reaches step 1 and raises `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: logging.Logger method not supported for non-export cases` (dev context: `transformers.configuration_utils` logger `.warning_once('`use_return_dict` is deprecated!...')`), so the run never trains. Cause: DPTrainer always patches with performance=True, which since #988 installs the fused loss-only causal-LM forward on all 17 `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM` families, and its `self.config.use_return_dict` read (cross_entropy.py:257-259) hits a transformers 5.15.1 deprecation property that logs - untraceable under the `fullgraph=True` chunk compiler, which has no fallback. Device-independent, since that line precedes the CUDA/CPU kernel branch. Same failure for Qwen2ForCausalLM. Disabling the patch (`performance_kernels_config={'fused_linear_cross_entropy': False}`) completes 3/3 steps, and Phi3ForCausalLM (not in the registry) completes as well, isolating the cause. Neutralizing only the deprecated property exposes a second, independent blocker in the portable chunked kernel: `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported` on the pybind builtin `torch._C._functorch.is_gradtrackingtensor` called from `_vmap_batch_factor` (_linear_ce_chunked.py:96 via `_tile_plan` :120). No privacy or numerical impact - the run aborts loudly - but `torch_compile` is documented as supported (docs/reference/transformers.md:218, docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:216) and is unusable with any registered HF family at default patch settings; existing compile tests miss it because they only compile `nn.Linear` and a hand-written non-HF `_TinyLM`.
